text: Bouhezza is never pressed or cut: the skin bag is filled in layers over weeks, whey seeps out through it, and the mass ripens in the bag under its own lactic flora. It has been granted a quality-sign recognition (geographical indication process) in Algeria.

steps.name: prepare skin
steps.note: The skin has its hair removed, is washed, treated with salt and juniper berry, turned inside out, rinsed, then left overnight with lben, a soured milk.

steps.name: fill
steps.note: The bag is filled with salted lben, preferably skimmed and low in acidity, to at least half; over several weeks more lben and salt are added, and the raw milk last.
The cheese is acidified, drained of whey and ripened together through the permeable skin.

processing.text: No starter; salted lben is added to the skin over weeks and the indigenous flora do the work, with yeasts and moulds at 5-6 log. Cloth bags are often used instead of skin today.
